items.title: FX Daily: Swiss franc becomes favourite funding currency
items.excerpt: The dollar remains bid as investors position for a hawkish FOMC tomorrow, if not a rate hike. And source stories that the Swiss National Bank will keep its policy rate unchanged at 0.00% until the end of 2027 hit the Swiss franc yesterday. Expect the franc to become the preferred funding currency and USD/CHF to lead the dollar higher if the Fed is…

items.title: British Pound futures erased gains ahead of BOE decision.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming of KKM Financial analyzes the recent selling pressure in British Pound futures, which have traded lower in seven of the last eight sessions. After reaching a mid-month peak of 1.355, the pound has staircased lower to give back all of its July gains, returning to the 1.328 opening level. Deming explains that shifting market expectations surrounding Thursday's Bank of England rate decision are driving this downward momentum. While a recent rally in crude oil prices previously sparked thoughts of a potential rate hike, markets are now broadly expecting the central bank to hold rates steady. Traders continue to position defensively as short-term sentiment shifts ahead of the critical policy announcement.

items.title: Equity Markets Rise on Easing Middle East Tensions.
items.excerpt: Watch Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners break down the latest market moves, including higher trending equities and metals. Crude oil sees a gap lower amid easing geopolitical tensions and reduced supply disruption risks in the Middle East. Plus, get the latest on Treasury yield pullbacks, upcoming U.S. Treasury auctions, and a massive slate of corporate earnings reports expected later today and tomorrow.

The sharp fall in oil prices is supporting EUR/USD, but downside risks remain unless a clear de-escalation path emerges. The Bank of England should remain on hold on…

items.excerpt: Markets are split about the Fed's move on Wednesday, and with no forward guidance, we don't expect that to change. In any case, we still take a more dovish view than markets, not just of the Fed, but also the Bank of England and European Central Bank. But with oil still the main driver, timing a material dovish turn remains…

items.title: Japanese Yen futures hit 40-year lows ahead of BOJ meeting.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners discusses the recent price action in September Japanese Yen futures as the market trades near a 40-year low. After falling 5.98% since the cycle high on May 6 and closing lower in 10 of the last 11 weeks, market participants remain alert to potential official action. Iaccino highlights recent comments from Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama signaling a readiness to intervene if necessary. He also looks ahead to the upcoming Bank of Japan policy meeting, where officials are widely expected to hold the benchmark rate at 1%, with economists largely projecting December as the most likely timing for the next rate hike.
items.author: CME Group

items.title: 10-Year yield jump and 36% hike chance press markets.
items.excerpt: Geopolitics and central bank policy intersect for the week of July 27, 2026. Tensions in the Middle East elevate risks for WTI Crude Oil futures, as potential shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz could push energy prices higher. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve convenes its policy meeting with futures pricing in roughly a 36% chance of an interest rate hike, despite expectations for a hold. With 10-Year Treasury yields up 11 bps, rate-sensitive assets across gold, equity index, and currency markets face critical catalysts alongside major earnings reports from tech giants.

items.title: Euro futures fell as ECB held rates steady.
items.excerpt: Euro futures experienced heightened volatility, initially climbing above 1.1430 before ultimately closing lower near 1.1375 following the latest European Central Bank decision. With the ECB holding rates steady and leaving the possibility of a September hike open, market focus quickly shifted to the Federal Reserve. The U.S. dollar surged as expectations for a rate hike at the upcoming July FOMC meeting jumped significantly, rising above 30 percent after sitting near zero just a week prior. This divergence in central bank outlooks continues to influence currency valuations. Additionally, broader market volatility remains elevated, driven by ongoing geopolitical events in the Middle East and crude oil prices approaching $100 per barrel. These rising energy costs are creating inflationary…

items.title: Rising yields and oil spikes more U.S. markets.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino covers the latest market moves as rising U.S. Treasury yields pressure stock index futures, pushing the Nasdaq, S P, Dow, and Russell lower. He analyzes the European Central Bank's decision to hold rates steady amid growing inflation and downward growth risks. Iaccino also examines the sudden climb in WTI crude oil prices following reported attacks on oil tankers in the Middle East and the resulting supply chain disruptions. Finally, he breaks down the heavy slate of upcoming corporate earnings and critical economic data, including manufacturing PMIs and U.S. new home sales, outlining what traders need to monitor next.
items.author: CME Group

items.title: Euro futures rise as ECB and Fed rate decisions approach.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the latest price action in Euro futures as the September contract bounces following four consecutive lower closes. With the ECB meeting approaching, markets are pricing high expectations for unchanged rates following cooled Eurozone inflation data. Meanwhile, the upcoming Federal Reserve meeting keeps the U.S. and European interest rate gap intact, with geopolitical conflict in the Middle East remaining a key variable for central bank outlooks.
items.author: CME Group

items.title: Stocks pull back while crude surges on geopolitical deadlock.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the morning market action as U.S. stock futures pull back and crude oil rises amid deadlocked U.S.-Iran peace negotiations. Meanwhile, gold gains ground, Treasury yields edge higher, and traders await key earnings from Alphabet and Tesla alongside the upcoming ECB rate decision.
items.author: CME Group

items.title: Euro futures fell for a 4th straight session near 1.14.
items.excerpt: Euro futures moved lower, closing near 1.14 to mark a fourth consecutive daily decline. Strength in the U.S. Dollar, fueled by uncertainty around Middle East tensions, oil prices, and Federal Reserve policy, continued to weigh on the currency. Market focus turns to the European Central Bank meeting later this week, where no policy changes are expected, though traders remain attentive to future rate path expectations. Meanwhile, CVOL index data shows declining euro volatility, and CFTC positioning data reveals that speculators expanded their net short euro positions for only the second time since March 2025.
